page: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz, provisioned with 8 physical cores delivering 16 vCPUs through simultaneous multithreading. Compute resources are paired with 128 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio, along with a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD for fast transient storage. The configuration includes no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-thread performance alongside solid multi-core execution. The instance scores in the top tier for Geekbench single-core (2767.0) and stress-ng single-core (3779.99), complemented by strong execution in single-threaded data compression benchmarks such as gzip (37.48 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.58 GB/sec). Multi-core benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core (15221.0) and PassMark CPU (32237.46), place the instance comfortably in the mid-range for its core class. Small-scale LLM prompt processing and text generation also show strong throughput, though throughput falls off on 7B and 70B models due to the absence of hardware accelerators.

The dense 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high clock speeds provide favorable cost efficiency for enterprise services where RAM capacity and per-core execution latency dictate cluster sizing. The bundled 945 GB NVMe local disk eliminates external disk latency for caching layers and temporary data stores, though production setups must consider that local NVMe disks are ephemeral. Workloads best aligned with the E16ads_v7 include in-memory key-value databases such as Redis, relational database engines, memory-intensive ETL pipelines, and high-performance compilation or processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 128 GB of RAM—delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio—and integrates a 945 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks demonstrate leading single-thread capability, reflected in top-tier results for single-core Geekbench, stress-ng, and data compression tests, while multi-threaded benchmarks demonstrate balanced compute capacity. The included high-speed NVMe storage and substantial memory footprint make this instance cost-effective for memory-heavy setups by consolidating database and cache footprints into fewer nodes. Microsoft Azure E16ads_v7 is well suited for running relational databases, Redis in-memory caches, analytics pipelines, and memory-bound transactional enterprise workloads.
